headline: High: Notion AI can read shared workspace content while Argo Workflows can move artifacts/parameters, creating default-path data leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt injection is lower because no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows has no documented direct ingestion of Notion AI outputs, and Notion AI is vendor-hosted with no host execution. The only plausible bridge is manual or workspace-mediated content transfer, so hijack risk exists but is not default. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF Argo outputs are copied into Notion pages and then reinterpreted as instructions
IF a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Label AI-generated text as untrusted in Notion pages
Require human review before reusing Argo-generated instructions
Separate instruction pages from data pages in Notion
Disable copy-paste of raw agent output into operational runbooks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI can access workspace pages and databases, while Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters and can egress to allowlisted endpoints. A shared workspace or copied artifacts can therefore expose sensitive content to Notion’s vendor backend in default use. The pairwise path is indirect but plausible, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Argo artifacts or parameters contain sensitive data and are pasted into Notion pages
IF the same workspace content is used as input to both agents
mitigations: Redact secrets before moving artifacts into Notion
Keep operational artifacts outside Notion workspace pages
Restrict Notion pages to non-sensitive summaries
Review allowlisted egress destinations for Argo jobs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows can call REST/gRPC APIs and egress on allowlists, while Notion AI is limited to vendor-hosted actions on workspace data and has no filesystem write or shell execution. Their write surfaces do not overlap directly, so conflict is limited unless an external orchestrator maps both onto the same mutable resource.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same API-backed resource
IF Argo job outputs are used to mutate Notion workspace content automatically
mitigations: Avoid granting both agents write access to the same resource
Use separate service accounts for workflow and knowledge tools
Add approval gates before any Notion write action
Log and diff all cross-system mutations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it can treat upstream text as authoritative unless humans verify it. Argo Workflows can generate artifacts and parameters that may become that upstream text. This creates a default-path cascade from Argo output into Notion answers, with moderate blast radius.
conditions: IF Argo-produced artifacts are imported into Notion as source material
IF Notion answers are used operationally without human verification
mitigations: Require citations for Notion answers derived from Argo outputs
Add a human review step before acting on Notion summaries
Mark Argo-generated pages as draft-only
Separate source-of-truth data from explanatory notes

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion vendor backends and downstream model providers, while Argo Workflows is open-source and allowlisted-egress only. If regulated data from Argo lands in Notion workspace content, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises from their interaction.
conditions: IF regulated data from Argo artifacts is copied into Notion workspace pages
IF the workspace’s retention or residency policy differs from the downstream model provider’s policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion pages
Document retention and residency for Notion AI use
Use de-identified summaries instead of raw records
Review whether the workspace data class is permitted in Notion
